links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of PREDICT versions on Dutch registry data versus observed 10-year survival
links.effect: Overall AUC 0.768 (v2.2) and 0.775 (v3.1); v3.1 overestimated OS by 1.9%, v2.2 underestimated by 1.6%; small differences varying by subgroup.
links.quote: Both PREDICT v2.2 and v3.1 accurately predict 10-year OS in Dutch breast cancer patients, with small differences between versions that vary by subgroup.

links.outcome: Performance across 36 subgroups by ER, HER2, age and tumour stage
links.effect: v3.1 generally outperformed v2.2 except age >75, where v2.2 was more accurate; in ER-/HER2- aged 50-75, v3.1 overestimated 1.5-2.8% and v2.2 underestimated 2.8-5.3%.
links.quote: Across subgroups, v3.1 generally outperformed v2.2 except in patients aged >75 years, where v2.2 provided more accurate estimates.

screen.reason: This study is an external validation of an established clinical risk prediction tool (PREDICT v2.2 and v3.1) on a nationwide registry cohort, assessing discrimination and calibration across demographic/clinical subgroups.
